zh.title: Joby 啟動自主飛行 Cessna Caravan 全美巡展
zh.summary: Joby 展開為期一個月的自主飛行示範巡展，涵蓋 10 個州 12 個停靠點
body: Joby Aviation 於 2026 年 9 月啟動為期一個月的「Electric Skies」計畫巡展，以改裝的 Cessna Grand Caravan（機型代碼 J208）展示其自主飛行系統在真實營運環境中的成熟度，並針對民用與國防物流應用進行示範。
巡展路線橫跨美國 10 個州，計劃停靠鳳凰城、沃斯堡、南卡羅來納州 Shaw 空軍基地、北卡羅來納州外灘與羅利、弗吉尼亞州 Stafford、華盛頓特區、肯塔基州路易維爾、堪薩斯州威奇托、奧克拉荷馬城、猶他州鹽湖城，最終在俄勒岡州波特蘭結束。
各站點皆有特定示範重點：鳳凰城著重國防、首批救援與貨運操作；沃斯堡在 Alliance 機場展示自主貨運；外灘靠近 Kitty Hawk 具象徵意義；北卡羅來納州配合 eLIFT-NC 計畫驗證醫療物流與緊急醫療響應；華盛頓特區測試複雜空域自主操作；路易維爾在 UPS Worldport 驗證貨運自動化；威奇托則為 Cessna 原廠 Textron Aviation 所在地。
Joby 指出 J208 已完成超過 400 架次、累積逾 800 小時的自動化飛行，涵蓋管制與非管制空域；其自主系統源自 2024 年收購的 Xwing 技術，並參與五州「uFLY 聯盟」在高海拔、沙漠與多變區域空域的數據蒐集。
創辦人兼執行長 JoeBen Bevirt 表示：「自主飛行能改變我們運送必需物資、應對緊急情況與支援軍人的方式」，強調巡展旨在展示飛機如何融入國家空域、服務社區並強化物流網絡。

en.title: Joby Launches Month‑Long Autonomous Cessna Caravan U.S. Tour
en.summary: Joby begins a 10‑state demonstration tour of its autonomous J208 Caravan, showcasing civil and defense logistics
body: Joby Aviation has begun a month‑long tour across the United States to demonstrate the capabilities of its autonomous aircraft, taking the technology from California to the East Coast and back through a series of stops in 10 states. The tour is part of Joby’s 2026 ‘Electric Skies’ programme and is designed to showcase the real‑world operational maturity of the company’s autonomous flight system and its potential applications in both civilian and defence operations.

The J208, a converted Cessna Grand Caravan equipped with Joby’s autonomous flight technology, will make stops including Phoenix, Fort Worth, Shaw Air Force Base in South Carolina, the Outer Banks and Raleigh in North Carolina, Stafford and Washington, D.C., Louisville, Wichita, Oklahoma City and Salt Lake City, before the tour concludes in Portland, Oregon.

Each location has a specific role: Phoenix will highlight defence, first‑responder and cargo‑operator applications; Fort Worth will focus on autonomous freight operations at Alliance Airport (AIA); the Outer Banks stop near Kitty Hawk marks the coast‑to‑coast leg; North Carolina will demonstrate healthcare logistics and rapid emergency medical response through the eLIFT‑NC initiative; Washington, D.C. will test autonomous operations in complex airspace; Louisville will showcase cargo automation at UPS Worldport; and Wichita, home of Textron Aviation, the original Caravan manufacturer, is also on the route.

Joby says the J208 has completed more than 400 flights and accumulated more than 800 hours of automated flight time in both controlled and uncontrolled airspace. The autonomy system originated with Xwing, a company acquired by Joby in 2024, and several western stops form part of the ‘uFLY coalition’, a five‑state partnership examining autonomous flight across challenging environments.

Founder and CEO JoeBen Bevirt said: “Autonomous flight can transform how we deliver essential supplies, respond to emergencies and support our servicemen and women. We have already demonstrated this technology in demanding military exercises. Now, we’re taking it across America to show how the aircraft can integrate into our national airspace to serve communities, strengthen our logistics networks and help keep people out of harm’s way.”
